newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins recover on US data, eye Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins recover on US data, eye Yeltsin.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices followed U.S. Treasuries up on Tuesday on reassuring news on December U.S. inflation, after easing on Tuesday in early trading on nervousness about President Boris Yeltsin's health.

Speculation Yeltsin's health may be worse than the Kremlin is admitting hit Russian debt prices earlier on Tuesday. The Kremlin plans its next bulletin on Yeltsin's health after his doctors meet today at 1400 GMT.

But prices recovered some of their losses when U.S. Treasuries, which affect all the emerging debt, rose on Tuesday after news of a 0.3 percent rise in December U.S. inflation, but only 0.1 percent minus food and energy.
"The U.S. data coincided with forecasts and the market has perceived it positively. The MinFin market is looking upwards," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kovzharov said.
"But those interested in Russia are awaiting news from the doctors' meeting," he added.
"Prices were falling on London rumours concerning Yeltsin's illness and his political future," a Moscow bank dealer said.
The fourth tranche had been hit the most, finding support at 58.00, dealers said.
